caption.verbatim: Figure 3: the relationship between incremental utility and investment

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 3: the relationship between incremental utility and investment
items.note: A hand-drawn illustration, not a plot of data: two arrow-headed axes meeting at a point slightly left of centre, the ordinate labelled U and the abscissa labelled x at their far ends, one smooth concave-then-flattening curve rising from below the abscissa to the upper right, and TWO DASHED RECTANGLES drawn from two points on the curve to the axes to mark an incremental step: the ordinate pair is labelled delta-U and the abscissa step is labelled delta-x. NO TICKS, NO NUMBERS, NO SCALE, NO GRIDLINE, NO LEGEND, and no value of any kind - the curve encodes concavity and nothing else, so the equation it illustrates (ROI = delta-U over delta-x, printed as equation (6)) is the only quantitative statement in the section. The small body type of the labels, delta-U left of the ordinate and delta-x below the abscissa, is the smallest text on the page. Captioned BELOW as 'Figure 3: the relationship between incremental utility and investment'; the sentence that precedes it, 'We can plot a figure to describe the relationship:', names nothing, and the figure is first NAMED ON THE NEXT PAGE in 'In Figure 3 and equation (6), delta-x is the incremental amount of the inputs triggered by the investment.'

caption.verbatim: Figure 4: flow chart of the LA_PSA_GT algorithm

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 4: flow chart of the LA_PSA_GT algorithm
items.note: A full-page vertical flowchart for the hybrid optimiser, drawn with plain rectangles, rounded terminals and two decision diamonds: Start, Initialize Lagrange multiplier, Construct Bound constrained problem, Initialize PSO parameters, Initialize the personal best particle and global best particle, Update the positions and velocities of the particles, Update the fitness the personal best particle and global best particle, Select the swarm previous best position as the initial point and update it by using Fletcher-Reeves conjugate gradient algorithm, the diamond PSO stopping criterion (NO arm loops back one box; YES arm falls through), the diamond Lagrange stopping criterion (NO arm loops back to the very first box from the left margin; YES arm falls through), Output f_gbest and g_best, End. Fifteen boxes and two nested loops, every arrow one-way and unlabelled except the two YES/NO pairs, no axes and no numbers. WHAT THE CHART DOES NOT SHOW is the inner detail the text spends four pages deriving: the conjugate-gradient step is collapsed into a single box, and the augmented-Lagrange update that the section is named for appears only as the first box and the second diamond. NO SENTENCE NAMES IT - the caption 'Figure 4: flow chart of the LA_PSA_GT algorithm' prints below the chart and the two definitions that follow it ('f_gbest is the maximum of the total ROI function', 'g_best is vector of investment amount per year') are the only prose that touches it.

A MATLAB figure: one heavy red curve that drops from about 6e20 at iteration 0 through 1, 0.8 and 0.3 by iteration 25 and flattens onto the abscissa from about iteration 60 out to 150, inside a full box frame with light vertical gridlines at 50, 100 and 150. The in-frame title is the single word 'fitness'; the ordinate is graduated 0 to 6 with a floating multiplier 'x 10^20' printed at its top; the abscissa is graduated 0, 50, 100 and 150 and CARRIES NO LABEL AT ALL, so the unit of the horizontal axis (iterations? function evaluations?) is never stated. No legend, no data label, no value printed, and no marker on the point the algorithm stops at. The curve is a step function in its first forty iterations, falling in flat treads, so it records the best-so-far value rather than a converging sequence. Untitled in the sense that 'fitness' names the quantity, not the plot, and NO SENTENCE NAMES THE FIGURE: the caption 'Figure 5: fitness of the algorithm' prints below it and the following paragraph discusses small investments without referring back.

note:
Paper 100, Team 47823, a Goodgrant Foundation strategy: rank 2977 colleges, keep 500, fit an ROI
function on earnings and graduation rate, and distribute a five-year budget by a particle-swarm search
under an augmented-Lagrangian constraint. Twenty-seven pages, sixteen measured regions over twelve of
them, resolving into FIVE FIGURE ROWS, SEVEN TABLE ROWS and FOUR EXCLUSIONS, with nothing unaccounted.

THE HEADING INDEX COLLAPSES ON THIS PDF. Its text layer writes one word per line, so every indexed
heading keeps only its first word - 'Data', 'Analysis', 'Results', 'Testing', 'Appendix' - and the
section labels recorded here are those indexed labels verbatim rather than the printed headings, which
are '1 Problem Statement', '4 Data Analysis and Focus Decision', '5.2.4 PCA Results', '8.1 Sensitivity
Analysis' and so on. The same defect empties the caption pass: it finds no caption group in the paper
at all, so every caption in this record was located by hand from its line position on the page.

Table 1 is the notation list - nine symbols from U to lambda,nu - and it defines nothing that the
model later needs to look up: k, the constant that becomes the subject of a whole sensitivity table,
has no row, and neither do the five yearly investment amounts.

Table 2 classifies the IPEDS variables by type and use, and it TURNS THE PAGE: its header and four
rows print at the foot of p5, its other nine rows and its caption at the head of p6. The left column is
three merged group cells, so the horizontal rules break inside the right column only. Variable names
keep their raw database spelling and mostly lose the space before the parenthesis
('UGDS_(the distribution by race)', 'PPTUG_EF(part-time ratio)').

Figures 1 and 2 are stock screenshots from the Foundation Center viewer, watermarked, with every value
printed at the bar end but no axis, no tick, no gridline and no scale on either. Figure 2 charts
recipient locations and prints, as its Source, the same 'subject:all' URL as Figure 1. Both are used to
justify the paper's focus: invest less in Health, Education and Human Services and in New York,
California, DC and Massachusetts.

Figure 3 is a hand-drawn curve of U against x with delta-x and delta-U marked by dashed rectangles and
no ticks, numbers or scale anywhere. Its section says 'We can plot a figure to describe the
relationship:' and does not name it; the figure is first named on the next page.

Figure 4 is a full-page flowchart of the LA_PSA_GT hybrid: fifteen boxes, two nested loops, UNLABELLED
arrows except the two YES/NO pairs, and the Fletcher-Reeves step the text spends pages on collapsed
into one box. Figure 5 is a MATLAB convergence curve titled simply 'fitness', with a floating
'x 10^20' multiplier on the ordinate, no abscissa label at all, and a step-shaped best-so-far trace.
Neither figure is named by any sentence.

Table 3 is the PCA shortlist, ten schools from 32.87 to 20.21, the only table in the paper with a rank
column. Tables 4 to 6 and the appendix list are all closed-box grids in the same style as Tables 1 to
3, which makes the paper's evidentiary tables and its notation list indistinguishable at a glance.

Table 4 prints the first ten rows of the recommending list with an ellipsis row and a merged footer
'Utilization rate of funds in each year(%)' carrying 99.60 99.79 99.63 99.71 99.69. The appendix
prints the same list to fifty rows and repeats the footer with slightly different wording. THE TWO
VERSIONS DISAGREE ON THE 't' COLUMN for all ten shared institutions while agreeing on every ROI, so
one of the two printings reports an integer that the other contradicts. 't' itself is never defined,
holds 2 to 6, and is headed by a bare italic letter.

Table 5 is the Gates comparison: ten well-known schools with Gates amounts, used to claim the model
duplicates nobody's focus. The check runs one way only - no Gates school appears in the model's list -
so the test passes by construction. 'Land-Grant Universities' is listed as though it were one college.

Table 6 is the k-sensitivity sweep and its caption is wrong: it says 'the standard deviation of the
investment amount', and the foot row is the plain mean of the five rows above it in each column. Its
'Year' column holds 1 to 5 - period indices, not years. It also turns the page, printing four rows on
p18 and two on p19.

The appendix list is titled rather than captioned ('Appendix 1: Recommending List'), is named by no
sentence, prints row 39 as 'Richard Bland College of the College of William and Mary' with the phrase
repeated, and has thirty-one of its fifty rows investing exactly 0.00 in at least one year.

Families: bar 2, line 2, flowchart-or-schematic 1, table-grid 7.
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: sixteen measured regions resolve into five figure rows, seven table rows and four exclusions, and every region is accounted for once [place.doc_order].

A table can turn the page: Table 2 and Table 6 each print their head on one page and their foot on the next, and the appendix list runs from p23 to p24, so three measured regions are heads or tails of a table recorded once elsewhere [table.continued].
A region can hold a piece of a formula rather than an exhibit: the p26 region is an equals sign and a root over two summations with no frame, no caption and no number [caption.numbering].

Two exhibits that answer one question can disagree: Table 4 and the appendix list share their first ten institutions and ROIs and print DIFFERENT integers under the undefined column 't' (4 5 3 5 3 6 5 5 6 5 against 4 5 3 4 3 5 4 4 5 4) [table.numeric_cols].

A caption can name a statistic the table does not print: Table 6 is captioned 'the standard deviation of the investment amount' and its foot row is the arithmetic MEAN of the five rows above it (10.49% = (12.18+9.09+10.88+7.64+12.67)/5) [caption.verbatim].

Two stock screenshots can cite one source: Figures 1 and 2 are the same viewer, and the Source URL printed under the location chart is byte for byte the subject-filtered URL printed under the subject chart [mention.style].

Headers can be left as variable names: 'INSTNM' stands over the institution column of every nine-column table, the year columns are headed only 1 to 5 with no year and no unit, and the column 't' holds integers 2 to 6 that no sentence defines [table.units_in_header].

Citation is thin and always unnumbered at the table: two figure rows are named by a sentence, Figure 3 only on the page after it prints, and every table is referred to as 'the table above' or not at all, while Figures 4 and 5, Table 1, Table 2 and the appendix list are named by nothing [mention.count].

tables.note: The paper's notation list: a black-filled header bar 'Notation | Meaning' over NINE body rows that run U (Social utility of the school), x (Amount of the investment), j (Time period (j =0,1,2,3,4,5)), m, M, N, k (MRS (marginal rate of substitution)), g (Graduation rate) and lambda,nu (Lagrange multiplier). CLOSED BOX: a rule at top and foot, rules between every pair of rows, vertical rules at both edges and between the two columns, so the nine rows are counted in ruled cells. Every entry is centred and italic, one symbol per row, and the header is white on black rather than ruled off. The caption 'Table 1: notation' prints BELOW and NO SENTENCE NAMES THE TABLE - the only pointer is the prose 'Here are the notations and their meanings in our paper:', which names nothing. Nine symbols are defined here and the model then uses quantities that appear in no row of it, among them the constant k that the paper later makes the subject of a whole sensitivity table.

tables.note: The comparison table for the duplicate-focus test: a header bar 'Rank | INSTNM | Investment amount (million)' over ten rows, Harvard University 24.14, University of Washington 16.42, Seattle University 15.80, Yale University 7.50, Texas Tech University 6.96, University of Michigan 6.85, Land-Grant Universities 4.95, University of Kentucky 4.50, Columbia University 3.78, Stanford University 3.25. CLOSED BOX, rules between every pair of rows and vertical rules between the three columns; the amounts carry two decimals and align on the point. It exists to support the claim that the model duplicates nobody's focus, and the test it supports is one-sided: the paper checks that no Gates school appears in its own list and never checks the reverse, so a list chosen to avoid those ten names passes by construction. 'Land-Grant Universities' is printed as if it were one institution, and the column header gives no currency. Captioned BELOW; referred to after the fact as 'In the table above, we can see that Gates Foundation invested mostly on those well-known schools like Harvard and Yale.'

mention.trail_sentence: From the table above, we can see that the influence of k is not very large

tables.note: The sensitivity sweep on the constant k, and it TURNS THE PAGE: four rows (periods 1 to 4) print at the foot of p18, the fifth row and the foot row print at the head of p19, so the measured region holds two of the seven printed rows. Five columns: a 'Year' column holding 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 - PERIOD INDICES, NOT YEARS - against four change columns headed k minus 10%, k minus 5%, k plus 5% and k plus 10%, all in per cent. CLOSED BOX throughout, rules between every pair of rows and vertical rules between all five columns. THE CAPTION AND THE CONTENT DO NOT MATCH: it reads 'Table 6: the standard deviation of the investment amount correspond to the change of MRS k', and the rows are percentage changes of the investment amount under a perturbation of k whose foot row 'Mean value' carries 10.49% 4.83% 4.80% 11.08% - the arithmetic mean of the five rows above it in each column, not a standard deviation, and a standard deviation printed beside the values it summarises would be a different quantity on a different scale. The column change under k-5% is the smallest everywhere and under k+10% the largest, which is the only pattern the table carries. Captioned BELOW; referred to afterwards as 'From the table above, we can see that the influence of k is not very large, and within the range we can bear.'

The full recommending list, ranks 1 to 50, under the title line 'Appendix 1: Recommending List': the same nine columns as Table 4 (Rank, INSTNM, ROI, a bare 't', then five unlabelled year columns), ranks 1 to 35 on this page and 36 to 50 with the merged foot row on the next, ROI falling from 2.22 to 0.02 and ending on a footer 'Utilization rate of funds of each year (%)' spanning Rank through t with 99.60 99.79 99.63 99.71 99.69. CLOSED BOX with vertical rules between all nine columns and rules between every pair of rows; two institution names wrap onto two lines and stay single rows; row 39 prints 'Richard Bland College of the College of William and Mary' with 'of the College of' repeated. THE TEN ROWS THIS TABLE SHARES WITH TABLE 4 CARRY DIFFERENT 't' VALUES, and the footer wording differs between the two printings ('in each year(%)' against 'of each year (%)'), so the appendix is a second, later version of the table rather than a longer copy of it. Fifteen of the fifty rows invest exactly 0.00 in one or more years, and thirty-one rows carry at least one zero, which the paper never remarks on. It is the only exhibit in the paper with a title rather than a caption, and no sentence names it.
